governing_text: ParagraphPlan refines the document plan down to paragraphs: after the Brief, the Composer binds one Move to each Leg and generates the Leg's paragraphs and their Waypoints through the same kind of feedback loop as the Brief's, and hands them to the Packet through a planning record, never directly. Move information may be used up to Waypoint generation and nowhere after it. It is not Reiter and Dale's microplanning: word choice, reference and sentence shape stay inside the one Writer call. [implemented-against: specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md "The ParagraphPlan stage", copied 2026-11-11]
licensed_by: kogaki#1375 -- owner decision 2026-10-14: Waypoint generation is its own stage after the Brief, named ParagraphPlan, with its own file and command; the ParagraphPlan file names the Brief it was made from and the Brief names nothing downstream; retries and limits follow the Brief's rules, `brief.call_limit_s` per call and `brief.unit_rounds` per unit, with no limit on the whole job. The Leg is the unit, with at most `brief.paragraphs_per_leg` paragraphs per Leg (kogaki#1777, owner decision 2026-11-10).
shared_text_note: ONE CRITERION, WRITTEN ONCE (kogaki#1452): where the planner row and the judge row carry one criterion, it is written here and both `judgment_point` strings name it as `{{shared:<name>}}`; `judgePrompt` (src/workflow/judge.mjs) substitutes it, and checks/check-schema-binds.sh refuses a sentence one row carries with words changed from another's. The `relation` gap of kogaki#1446 sat in exactly such a difference.

shared_text.operation_is_performed: A Segment's `operation` is an operation performed on a part of the Leg's `text`, never a point to state.
shared_text.manner_is_not_content: A Segment's `manner`, where it carries one, names how the step is realised and is never part of what the Waypoint says.
shared_text.join_is_a_type: A `join` is one word naming how a paragraph's first Waypoint stands to the paragraph before it, never a sentence, from a closed set: `consequence` -- this paragraph follows from what the previous one established, `grounds` -- this paragraph gives the reason for what the previous one asserted, `contrast` -- this paragraph sets its matter against the previous one's, `elaboration` -- this paragraph carries the previous one's matter further or in more detail, `summary` -- this paragraph draws the preceding paragraphs together, or `none` -- this paragraph opens on its own matter and no connective is owed.
shared_text.cast_is_a_set: A `cast` is a map on each `point` Waypoint naming the shape its sentences take, never content, each key true or absent, from a closed set: `terse` -- one short statement given at once, taking no elaboration after it, `plain` -- laid down without support, ground or qualification, `hedged` -- offered as a guess or forecast rather than asserted, `chained` -- a run of parallel items or alternatives inside one sentence, `asked` -- put as a question that takes no lead-in, `voiced` -- spoken in a named voice, the first person, an invitation, or words reported as another's, `instanced` -- one recognisable instance named and left without comment, `dated` -- each instance placed in time, or `figured` -- asserted as a likeness or a figurative identification.
shared_text.takes_and_leaves: A `takes` or `leaves` entry is a `kind` and a `what`, the kind one of `answer` (a question raised, to be answered), `explain` (a term named, to be explained), `carry` (a base's structure, to be carried onto the subject) or `apply` (a principle given, to be applied to a case).
shared_text.analogue_is_the_mapping: Where the input carries `analogy_you_must_draw_from`, every analogue a paragraph names is that base domain or one of its counterparts, and a paragraph naming any other analogue does not fit.

criteria.note: THE ROWS ARE NAMED CRITERIA UNDER A BOUND (kogaki#1511, owner decision 2026-10-22). Each row's `judgment_point` is one lead line, then one line per criterion or step as `- <NAME>: <one sentence>`, then the shared text and the verdict, each shared block one sentence; a criterion carries no example, no run date and no Issue number, and a pointer rides beside it as its own line. The judge row's criteria are not written here: they are the axes of src/paragraph-plan-axes.json, rendered by its `{{axes}}` token and named in the registry's order (kogaki#1533). `criteriaFailures` in src/paragraph-plan.mjs reads the rendered rows against the names, `words_max` per criterion and `point_words_max` over the whole rendered judgment point, `start` refuses a row that fails, and checks/check-paragraph-plan.sh case (s) asserts the same. A change to either row names the criterion it changes and shows its text after the change, in its Issue.

judge.note: Every job unit of this stage is a headless session, a `claude -p` child that runs with no tools, spawned by the shared Detached Job supervisor (src/workflow/detached-job.mjs) with the binary the start act resolved. `model` NAMES THE BRIEF'S SETTING, `brief.judge_model`, because the owner decided this stage follows the Brief's rules rather than carrying settings of its own. `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI` replaces the resolved binary FOR FIXTURES ONLY.

job.note: ONE JOB UNIT PER LEG, in Reader Path order, and the two bounds are the Brief's own settings (kogaki#1375): a call running past `brief.call_limit_s` is stopped and spends one round, a refused answer spends one, an unreadable answer is asked again without spending one, and a unit that has spent `brief.unit_rounds` stops naming its Leg and the paragraph its last refusal named. There is no limit on the whole job. Each round makes two calls: `paragraph_plan_unit` binds one paragraph Move to the Leg and writes its paragraphs, at most `brief.paragraphs_per_leg` (kogaki#1777), and `paragraph_plan_judge_unit` judges them against the bound Move. A refusal of the whole Leg is put back into the next round's prompt verbatim; a refusal naming a paragraph is retried at that paragraph alone (`site_retry`, kogaki#1642). THE LEGS ARE INDEPENDENT (kogaki#1641, owner decision 2026-10-31): `unit_isolation` tells the shared supervisor that one Leg's death ends that Leg alone, its siblings finishing on their own merits; a finished Leg is kept in the run directory the tick its judge passes it; and a later run on the same Brief carries every kept Leg and plans only the Legs left unfinished.

site_retry.note: THE RETRY IS SCOPED TO THE PARAGRAPH THE REFUSAL NAMED (kogaki#1642, owner decision 2026-10-31). A judge's `does-not-fit` or a validator refusal naming one paragraph keeps the round's record as the Leg's standing record and asks `paragraph_plan_site_unit` for that one paragraph; the paragraphs the judge passed are not composed again. The Leg's Move is held at every site (kogaki#1777); a judge refusal on a binding axis, `TAKEN` or `LEFT`, refuses the Leg's Move, and the whole Leg is composed again by `paragraph_plan_unit`, which may bind another Move. An answer repeating a refused paragraph at the site is refused before the judge. The judge is then asked for the changed paragraphs and the join after them, its other verdicts carried. `brief.unit_rounds` is read per site, the Leg call's first round counting at every site, and `leg_revisions` bounds the site retries of one Leg. The supervisor runs the loop (src/workflow/site-retry.mjs) when a job declares it; the Brief's jobs declare none.

analogy_mapping.note: THE OPENING STEP (kogaki#1778, owner decision 2026-11-10): one call before the first Leg unit, over the Brief's `structure` and the Persona, run as a one-unit Detached Job in the run directory's `analogy/`; `validateAnalogyMapping` (src/paragraph-plan-analogy.mjs) reads the answer back, a refusal is put into the next round verbatim until `brief.unit_rounds` is spent, and the mapping is written at the top of `paragraph-plan.yaml` under `analogy`. Every Leg bound to an analogy Move (one whose `takes` or `leaves` carries a `carry` entry) is handed it; a Leg bound to no analogy Move reads nothing of it.
analogy_mapping.judgment_point: choose ONE base domain for the whole article, a domain the reader in `persona` already holds from `persona.prior_knowledge`, in which the system of `structure` holds: map EVERY Role of `structure.roles` to its counterpart in the base domain, and EVERY relation of `structure.relations` and every higher-order relation of `structure.higher_order`, `structure.apex` among them, to the base-domain relation it corresponds to, each counterpart one noun phrase or one sentence of the base domain. Prefer the domain that carries the apex's higher-order relation and not only one relation. Where no domain the reader holds carries the system, answer `none` with one sentence saying why no base domain fits.
analogy_mapping.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT -- `version` "1" and either `base_domain` (`{ "name": <a short name>, "description": <one sentence> }`), `roles` (one `{ "role": <the Role's id>, "counterpart": <text> }` per Role) and `relations` (one `{ "relation": <the relation's id>, "counterpart": <text> }` per relation and higher-order relation), or `none` (<one sentence>) alone
analogy_mapping.refusal: a record leaving a Role, a relation or the apex without a counterpart, naming it; a counterpart for an id the structure does not carry; a key the shape does not declare; `none` with no reason or beside a mapping. The next round receives the refused record beside its refusal, both verbatim.

paragraph_plan_unit.note: The first call of every round (kogaki#1375). It carries the second-pass judgment kogaki#1359 put inside the compose job, moved out of it: the Move binding is judged here, after the Brief is adopted, and its result never reaches the Brief. The Leg is the unit (kogaki#1777): one Move per Leg, and its paragraphs. `src/paragraph-plan.mjs` renders this row through the shared `judgePrompt` renderer up to the input marker and appends one Leg's own input below it; `validateParagraphPlanUnit` reads the answer.
paragraph_plan_unit.judgment_point:
plan the paragraphs of ONE Leg, `leg_you_must_plan` in the input, from five inputs and nothing else (`leg_you_must_plan`, `paragraphs_at_most`, `paragraph_moves_you_may_bind`, `persona` and `terms_this_leg_introduces`), taking these steps:
- BIND: Bind one Move from `paragraph_moves_you_may_bind` for the whole Leg whose `takes` entries are each met, the kind as a word and the `what` by sense, by the Leg's `prior_knowledge` or a relation of its `the_reader_has_been_told`, and whose Segments can carry its `text`, or answer `move: null` with a `rationale` naming the entry no Move takes up.
- PARAGRAPHS: Write the Leg's `paragraphs`, one or more and never more than `paragraphs_at_most`, each shaped whole by the bound Move's Segments, a later paragraph only where the one before cannot carry the rest of the Leg's `text`.
- MAP: Where the Leg carries a `structure`, bind a Move whose Segments carry its relations and then its higher-order relation, and where it carries `move` and `table` too, keep that `move` and write its Waypoints in the table's expressions, each expression in one of them and no Role id outside one.
- TERMS: Name a term of `terms_this_leg_introduces` in the `introduces` of at most one paragraph, the first in the Leg to use it, with its meaning (the input's, or yours where it is `null`), and only where that paragraph's Waypoints give the meaning, a term used without one named in no paragraph.
- DIVIDE: Write each paragraph's Waypoints one per Segment of the bound Move, in its order, each the step its Segment's `operation` performs toward the Leg's `text`.
- EXPLAIN: A Waypoint may explain or illustrate the Leg's `text` in words and examples of your own.
- CONSISTENT: No Waypoint contradicts the Leg's `text` or breaks the progression toward it.
- NO NEW FACT: No Waypoint states or implies a claim about the article's subject that the Leg's `text` and its `claims` do not make.
- ORDER: A Segment's `relation` is carried by the order of the Waypoints, and no Waypoint states it.
- FORM: Give each Waypoint a `point`, one sentence stating what its paragraph says and never what the paragraph does to its reader, with `serves` naming Strands of its paragraph's `materials` so that every one is served, except where its Segment's `operation` acts on the reader's reading, where it carries `performs` naming the operation alone with no clause stating what the reader then takes.
- JOIN: On every paragraph after the first, choose its `join` as the word the first Waypoint bears toward the paragraph before it, `contrast` or `none` where it defers what the previous paragraph leaves open, and give the first paragraph no `join`.
- CAST: Give each `point` Waypoint a `cast` setting true each key its Segment's `manner` bears, and `{}` where the Segment carries no `manner`.
- LEAVE: Every `leaves` entry of the bound Move is taken up by a later paragraph of this Leg or is in the Leg's `leaves_for_next_leg`, and a `carry` is taken up by the next paragraph.
{{shared:operation_is_performed}} {{shared:manner_is_not_content}} {{shared:join_is_a_type}} {{shared:cast_is_a_set}} {{shared:takes_and_leaves}} The Move's `takes`, `leaves`, `breaks` and `segments` and what the reader has been told decide the plan and are never stated in a Waypoint or a join. Word choice, reference and sentence shape beyond `cast` are not planned here; they stay with the Writer.
paragraph_plan_unit.input_shape: ONE plan record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT -- `version` "1", the `leg_id` of the Leg in the input, `move` (a Move id from the library, bound for the whole Leg, or null), `rationale` (one sentence: why this Move fits this Leg), and `paragraphs`, one or more and at most `paragraphs_at_most`, in order, each the paragraph-level Leg schema (kogaki#1639): `{ "paragraph": <its 1-based number>, "materials": [<Strand id>, ...] (Strands of the Leg's `claims`), "purpose": <one sentence, a verb about the reader>, "depends_on": [<an earlier paragraph's number of this Leg>, ...], "rationale": <one sentence: why this paragraph comes here>, "introduces": [ { "term": <a term of terms_this_leg_introduces>, "meaning": <one line> }, ... ], "re-activate": [<`<paragraph> term <term>` or `<paragraph> claim <Strand id> as <one plain sentence>`, an earlier paragraph of this Leg>, ...], "journeys": [ { "strand": <Strand id>, "use": <the Leg's use>, "meaning": <the Leg's> }, ... ] (only where the paragraph places one of the Leg's `journeys`), "join": <one word: consequence | grounds | contrast | elaboration | summary | none>, "paragraph_waypoints": [ { "point": <one sentence>, "serves": [<Strand id>, ...], "cast": { <a key of the set>: true, ... } } | { "performs": <one sentence: the Segment's operation on the reader's reading, in your words> }, ... ] }` -- no paragraph carries `move`, which is the Leg's, or `why`, retired for `rationale`, and neither the record nor a paragraph carries `reader_state_before`, `reader_state_after`, `obligations` or `discharges` (kogaki#1701) -- each paragraph's `paragraph_waypoints` one per Segment of the bound Move and carrying at least one `point` entry; `performs` stands in place of `point` and `serves` only for a Segment whose `operation` acts on the reader's reading (kogaki#1448); `join` on every paragraph after the first, and absent from the first; a Waypoint carries no `manner` -- a Segment's `manner` is an input to this call and is copied onto no Waypoint (kogaki#1585); every `point` Waypoint carries `cast`, `{}` where no key is set, and a `performs` one carries none (kogaki#1695)
paragraph_plan_unit.refusal: a record naming another leg_id; a record carrying `waypoints`, one entry per Brief Waypoint, refused by name (kogaki#1777); `paragraphs` empty, or carrying more paragraphs than `paragraphs_at_most`, naming the Leg (kogaki#1777); a key the record does not declare, and the retired `why`, `reader_state_before`, `reader_state_after`, `obligations` and `discharges` on the record or a paragraph, each by name (kogaki#1701); a `move` naming no Move in the library; a `rationale` under four words; a paragraph carrying `move`; a paragraph numbered out of order; a paragraph with no `materials`, or one naming a Strand no Claim of the Leg names, no `purpose`, no `depends_on` or one naming this or a later paragraph, no `introduces` or one naming a term the Leg does not introduce, no `re-activate` or a line outside the two forms or naming this or a later paragraph or a term or Strand that paragraph does not carry, or a `journeys` entry the Leg does not carry; a term introduced by two paragraphs (kogaki#1639); a paragraph whose Waypoints are not one per Segment of the bound Move; a Waypoint with an empty point, an empty `serves`, a `serves` naming a Strand its paragraph's `materials` does not name, or any key but `point`, `serves` and `cast` -- or, for a `performs` Waypoint, an empty `performs` or any key beside it (kogaki#1448); a `point` Waypoint with no `cast`, a `cast` that is not a map, a key outside the set or a value that is not a boolean, each named, or a `cast` on a `performs` Waypoint (kogaki#1695); a paragraph none of whose Waypoints carries a `point`; a Strand of a paragraph's `materials` that no Waypoint serves; a `join` on the first paragraph, or a paragraph after the first which carries no `join`, an empty one, or one that is not one word of the set (kogaki#1477); a Waypoint stating what the paragraph does to its reader, named by its number and why. `move: null` is a judgment, not malformed output: the unit is refused `no_paragraph_move_fits` naming the Leg, and asked again with the sentence until `brief.unit_rounds` is spent. A BOUND MOVE THAT DOES NOT FILL A ROLE THIS STAGE NEEDS (`segments` or `breaks`) is not a refusal of your answer: the stage stops, naming the Move and the role, and nothing is defaulted. The next round receives the refused record beside its refusal, both verbatim (kogaki#1438).
paragraph_plan_unit.governing: SPEC-draft-pipeline, the ParagraphPlan stage and the Move boundary; kogaki#1375

paragraph_plan_judge_unit.note: The second call of every round (kogaki#1375), run by the supervisor's judge phase once `validateParagraphPlanUnit` has passed the first call's record. `src/paragraph-plan.mjs` renders this row through `judgePrompt` up to the input marker; `paragraphPlanJudgePrompt` appends the Leg's input and `paragraphPlanJudgeVerdict` reads the answer. A `does-not-fit` on any paragraph is a refusal of the round, and its sentence is put into the next round's first call.
paragraph_plan_judge_unit.input_shape: ONE verdict record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT -- `version` "1", the `leg_id` of the Leg in the input, and `verdicts`, one per paragraph in order: `{ "paragraph": <its 1-based number>, "verdict": "fits" | "does-not-fit", "why": <one sentence> }`
paragraph_plan_judge_unit.refusal: a record carrying no `verdicts` array, or naming another leg_id; a verdict outside the closed set; a paragraph carrying no verdict, or two, or verdicts out of order; a `why` under four words -- each of these is this judge's own malformed output, and the same prompt is asked again. `does-not-fit` is a verdict, not malformed output: the round is refused with it and the plan is generated again. The next round receives the refused record beside its refusal, both verbatim (kogaki#1438).

paragraph_plan_site_unit.note: The site call (kogaki#1642): asked for ONE paragraph after a refusal named it, by the supervisor's site loop, never for the whole Leg. `paragraphPlanSitePrompt` renders this row up to the input marker and appends the site's input; `validateParagraphPlanSite` reads the answer.
paragraph_plan_site_unit.judgment_point:
repair the ONE paragraph a refusal named, `paragraph_you_must_plan` in the input, and only it, taking these steps:
- READ: Read every entry of `refused_here` and the refusal beside it, and change what each refusal names.
- WRITE: `purpose`, `rationale` and every `point` describe the paragraph and its reader, and carry no word of the refusal, the attempt, the shape of the record or any rule by name.
- HOLD: Write the paragraph's Waypoints under the Leg's `bound_move`, one per Segment in its order, and name no Move, since the Move is the Leg's.
- BESIDE: Read `paragraphs_beside`, the Waypoints of the paragraphs before and after this one, and restate none of them.
- KEEP: Carry `terms_this_paragraph_introduces` and `re_activations_this_paragraph_carries` on the paragraph unless a refusal names them.
{{shared:operation_is_performed}} {{shared:manner_is_not_content}} {{shared:join_is_a_type}} {{shared:cast_is_a_set}} {{shared:takes_and_leaves}} {{shared:analogue_is_the_mapping}} An answer that repeats a refused paragraph, or restates a refused paragraph's Waypoints word for word in order under any other change, is refused before it is judged. Word choice, reference and sentence shape beyond `cast` are not planned here; they stay with the Writer.
paragraph_plan_site_unit.input_shape: ONE paragraph AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT, the paragraph-level Leg schema (kogaki#1639) of `paragraph_plan_unit`'s `paragraphs` entry: `{ "paragraph": <the input's number>, "materials": [...], "purpose": ..., "depends_on": [...], "rationale": ..., "introduces": [...], "re-activate": [...], "join": <one word, on every paragraph after the first>, "paragraph_waypoints": [...] }` -- no `move`, nothing of another paragraph and nothing of another Leg
paragraph_plan_site_unit.refusal: a paragraph numbered for another paragraph; a paragraph carrying `move`, by name (kogaki#1777); a paragraph the Leg call's paragraph rules refuse; a paragraph repeating a refused one -- after a judge's refusal the same `paragraph_waypoints` and `join`, after a validator's the same paragraph whole -- refused as a repeat; Waypoints whose `point` or `performs` text equals a refused paragraph's in order, refused as a restatement naming the unchanged points (kogaki#1651); a `purpose` or `rationale` carrying `refus`, `attempt`, `kogaki#` or a backticked field name, naming the field. Each refusal spends this paragraph's round and is put into the next site call's `refused_here` beside the answer it refused.
paragraph_plan_site_unit.governing: SPEC-draft-pipeline, the ParagraphPlan stage, the site retry; kogaki#1642
